title: Quantum Relative Entropy, Data Processing, and Strong Subadditivity

items.title: Inverse compression for a positive operator
items.statement: For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces H,K, a linear isometry V:H→K, a positive-definite T on K, and s≥0, V†(T+sI_K)⁻¹V ⪰ (V†TV+sI_H)⁻¹.
items.strategy: Use the variational characterization of a positive inverse and restrict its maximization to the isometric image of H.

items.title: The resolvent proof of the compression inequality for minus the logarithm
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional positive-definite operator T and an isometry V, −log(V†TV) ⪯ V†(−log T)V, where log is the natural spectral logarithm.
items.strategy: Integrate the inverse-compression inequality against the finite-matrix resolvent formula for −log, using finite cutoffs and operator-norm convergence.

items.title: The finite relative-modular operator identity
items.statement: For positive-definite A,B on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, the Hilbert–Schmidt operator Δ_{B,A}=L_B R_{A⁻¹}, with L_B(X)=BX and R_{A⁻¹}(X)=XA⁻¹, is positive definite and ⟨−log(Δ_{B,A})A^{1/2},A^{1/2}⟩_{HS}=D(A∥B).
items.strategy: Diagonalize A and B separately, use matrix-unit eigenoperators for Δ, and sum the resulting finite eigenvalue expression.

items.title: Common-support regularization of finite quantum relative entropy
items.statement: For finite-dimensional positive semidefinite A,B and ε↓0, D(A+εI∥B+εI) tends to D(A∥B), including +∞ exactly when supp A is not contained in supp B.
items.strategy: Diagonalize B, separate its kernel contribution, and use continuity of t log t at zero and ε|log ε|→0.

items.title: Joint convexity of finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy
items.statement: For a finite family of positive semidefinite pairs (A_i,B_i) and weights λ_i≥0 summing to one, D(Σ_i λ_iA_i∥Σ_i λ_iB_i)≤Σ_i λ_iD(A_i∥B_i), with the support-sensitive extended value convention.
items.strategy: Prove the positive-definite case with a Hilbert–Schmidt isometry and the proved −log compression inequality; extend to semidefinite pairs by common support regularization.

items.title: The finite Weyl twirl is the normalized partial trace
items.statement: For dim K=d≥1 and every operator R on H⊗K, d⁻²Σ_{p,q=0}^{d−1}(I_H⊗X^pZ^q)R(I_H⊗X^pZ^q)†=(Tr_K R)⊗I_K/d, where X is the cyclic shift and Z is the phase operator on an ordered orthonormal basis of K.
items.strategy: Expand in matrix units; phase averaging kills off-diagonal units and shift averaging replaces each diagonal unit by I_K/d.

items.title: Isometric invariance of finite quantum relative entropy
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional isometry V and positive semidefinite A,B, D(VAV†∥VBV†)=D(A∥B), including the extended support convention.
items.strategy: Transport the supports through V and use equality of the nonzero spectra and trace pairings.

items.title: Data processing of finite quantum relative entropy under partial trace
items.statement: For finite-dimensional spaces H,K with dim K≥1 and positive semidefinite A,B on H⊗K, D(Tr_K A∥Tr_K B)≤D(A∥B), with extended values.
items.strategy: Average the finite Weyl conjugates, apply joint convexity and unitary invariance, then cancel the common maximally mixed tensor factor spectrally.

items.title: Data processing for finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy
items.statement: For every finite-dimensional completely positive trace-preserving map Φ and positive semidefinite A,B, D(Φ(A)∥Φ(B))≤D(A∥B), with the extended support convention.
items.strategy: Apply the finite Stinespring dilation, isometric invariance, and the partial-trace inequality; treat infinite inputs in the extended order.

items.title: Strong subadditivity of finite-dimensional quantum entropy
items.statement: For every finite-dimensional tripartite state ρ_ABC, S(AB)+S(BC)≥S(B)+S(ABC).
items.strategy: Apply partial-trace data processing to (ρ_ABC,ρ_A⊗ρ_BC), establish support inclusion, then identify both divergences with finite mutual information.

items.strategy: Use the finite entropy identity for conditional mutual information, then apply strong subadditivity with C as the conditioning register.

items.title: A finite POVM defines a finite quantum-to-classical channel
items.statement: For a finite POVM (M_y)_{y∈Y} on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex space H, the map M(X)=Σ_y tr(M_yX)|y⟩⟨y| from L(H) to L(C^Y) is completely positive and trace-preserving.
items.strategy: Resolve each positive effect spectrally, build explicit Kraus operators into the outcome register, and verify every finite ancillary amplification and trace normalization.

items.title: The finite Holevo measurement bound
items.statement: For a finite ensemble {(p_x,ρ_x)} and every finite POVM measurement Y, I(X;Y)≤χ({p_x,ρ_x})=S(Σ_xp_xρ_x)−Σ_xp_xS(ρ_x), with zero-probability labels omitted.
items.strategy: Prove branch support inclusion, identify χ with the average relative entropy to the ensemble mean, apply channel data processing to each branch, and average.

title: Quantum Relative Entropy, Data Processing, and Strong Subadditivity — Examples

items.title: Qubit dephasing decreases quantum relative entropy
items.statement: For a qubit, the dephasing channel Δ(X)=|0⟩⟨0|X|0⟩⟨0|+|1⟩⟨1|X|1⟩⟨1| strictly decreases D(|+⟩⟨+|∥diag(3/4,1/4)) and maps the orthogonal pure-state pair |+⟩⟨+|,|−⟩⟨−| to the same maximally mixed state.
items.strategy: Write the Kraus operators for dephasing, compute the four finite spectra, and separately check the support-edge divergence.

items.title: Strong subadditivity for a pure GHZ tripartite state
items.statement: For the GHZ state (|000⟩+|111⟩)/√2, each one-register entropy and each complementary two-register entropy is ln 2, while the total entropy is 0; strong subadditivity holds strictly.
items.strategy: Compute reduced density spectra explicitly and use the Schmidt decomposition to explain complementary-spectrum equality.

items.title: Fidelity and trace-distance inequalities do not imply QRE data processing
items.statement: The implication “a map preserves root fidelity and contracts trace distance, therefore it contracts quantum relative entropy” is false for arbitrary maps: on diagonal qubit states a nonlinear map preserves root fidelity and contracts trace distance yet sends one finite classical relative entropy to +∞; the map is not CPTP.
items.strategy: Use an angle-shift nonlinear map on diagonal binary laws and compute its metric action, support loss, and a separate noncommuting pure-state pair.
